Today was a really good day to be an Arsenal fan. 

Leica M6 + Kodak Tri-X 400.
@ivysublime.bsky.social + natural light + Kodak Tri-X 400.

Portraiture with @ivysublime.bsky.social and Tri-X 400. I love everything about it, including the grain, and now I’m wondering what I’m going to do with the six rolls of 100 speed film in my refrigerator. Lit with a gridded beauty dish. ￼
Living the concrete stairwell cliche, in glorious Tri-X 400. Absent from this photo: any amount of handwringing about whether the sky is the ”right” shade of blue given the film stock.

Kodak Gold 200 + Leica M6. Unlike b&w film, I’m finding it shockingly easy to deviate from what you get out of the native emulsion when working with color. I have early edits where the tones here are more realistic, but that erases what Gold brings to the table.

Dappled sunlight is my new oeuvre. The last several photos look like throw-aways, but they were test shots with my new Leica M6 classic and I’m happy to say the meter checked out. Taken on Tri-X, natch.
Chiaroscuro, Tri-X style (oh, and a Leica M6 + Voigtlander 35mm Nokton 1.4 II).

I’m having mixed feelings about my 1st foray into medium format. Try as I might I can’t seem to get a sharp scan from my Epson V600. More experimentation is in my future.

More of the Claire/Tri-X pairing. This one was taken with my Leica M6, so it’s instantly “art.”

The Mercantile Center (home of the Hillsborough Galley of Arts) during golden hour. Taken on Kodak Gold 200.

I’m still feeling very “meh” about color film. It’s too malleable and eager to please. You can’t trust it. B&W is steadfast, reliable. You know where you stand with B&W.

Summer is here and it is time to lean into my North Carolina Summer Heat Mitigation strategy: a shaved head.

My M6 is out for a CLA and I miss her so much 😢

When I was studying photography in college (it was my first major) I had a professor whose kink was dynamic range. For every assignment, they said our submission must have a white, a black, and something like 14 shades of grey.

They would be extremely proud of this image. Taken in Tri-X.

The arrow led to nowhere. 1/10. Would not follow again. 

Contrasty goodness courtesy of Tri-X.
@ivysublime.bsky.social + Tri-X. Name a more iconic duo. I’ll wait 🤪
